5. Trial Court decreed the suit. While passing the judgment in the operative portion of it the trial Court ordered that the document is also cancelled. 

 6. Defendant took Title Appeal 101 of 1988. The appeal has been contested by the two daughters of the original plaintiff, as he expired by this time, against their own brother. The appellate Court also decided the litigation in favour of the plaintiffs by dismissing the appeal and upholding the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Hence the present Rule has been issued at the instance of the defendant son against the father now full sisters. 

 "For relief sought by way of cancellation of a document a kabala or a decree, section 39 is applicable. Main question now is, whether the relief of cancellation is a consequential relief or an independent relief. Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act does not specifically provide for cancellation of a document but it is section 39 of the Act which specifically provide for cancellation of any written instrument which includes both a deed of transfer and a decree. Section 39 provides for declaration of nullity of a written instrument in its words ''adjudge it so ''void'', it also provides that the court in the discretion may order the instrument when adjudged void to be delivered up or cancelled, From the provision it is obvious that the declaration of nullity is the main and substantive relief, whereas cancellation of the instrument is a consequential relief." 

 17. High Court Division under section 115 of CPC is empowered to pass necessary order to uphold the legal remedy to be given to the litigant, in appropriate cases in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record and can act even suo motu (See 36 DLR (AD) 1; 16 DLR (SC) 155 and 27 DLR 55). Accordingly, the judgments and decrees of the courts below are rectified only to the extent that the document in question is legal and valid one in respect of transfer of 0.30 acres land, but it is void and illegal in respect of the remaining portion of the land being 1.42 1/2 acres and the suit is decreed in part accordingly. 

 18. In the result, the Rule is discharged with the aforesaid modification of the judgments and decree of the courts below.
